comment: Per-resort corrections applied by pipeline/normalize_osm.py (ADR-036). See whistler-blackcomb.overrides.json for the format. Summit West, Summit Central and Summit East on one map: one ski area joined on snow by the Inter-Summit crossover trails, which the resort's Summit Shuttle page (summitatsnoqualmie.com/summit-shuttle) calls the easiest way between Summit West, Central and East ('ski or snowboard via our Summit-90 Crossover Trails') and its trail maps (summitatsnoqualmie.com/trail-maps) draw: the Upper Central to West Crossover and the Lower Crossover between West and Central, the East Crossover and the Lower Crossover between Central and East. Alpental, across Interstate 90, is joined to them by no lift or trail (the shuttle page: free bus transportation between the Summit areas and Alpental, its crossovers only between West, Central and East; Alpental's trail map: 'Shuttle or drive to Summit West, Central, East'), so it has its own map (alpental.overrides.json) by the owner's rule of 2026-11-14, which retired the combined map summit-at-snoqualmie-v1. Nothing of this map is reached only by shuttle or road. The ski area is way/1361868120 (Three Summits: Summit West, Central and East in one polygon, 3.94 km2). OpenStreetMap has no polygon of its own for Central or East: its Summit West polygon (way/1499174311) lies inside Three Summits, and relation/20445212, Three Summits with Summit West as its inner ring, is not a clean Central and East polygon (Summit West's ring leaves Three Summits' outline for about 240 m2 near the Summit West base), so Three Summits stands for the three areas. Listed neighbours in resorts.json: Alpental (relation/6855067) and Alpental Backcountry (relation/6855066, the Alpental Back Bowls), a separate ski area of the same resort on its own map, and the Sahalie Ski Club (relation/6447055), a private club with its own rope tow. Alpental's backcountry couloirs on Snoqualmie Mountain (Slot, Snot and Crooked) and the Chair Peak North Face Descent lie in no polygon and more than 250 m from Alpental's, so the neighbour rule would keep them here out of bounds: they are hidden below (the alpental pack draws them). Every named run and lift checked on 2026-11-14 against the resort's three current Summit trail maps (summitatsnoqualmie.com/trail-maps: the Summit West, Summit Central and Summit East maps, rated Easiest, More Difficult and Most Difficult; JPEGs of 3000 by 1508 px, read tile by tile) and its lift and trail report (summitatsnoqualmie.com/mountain-report, whose data, /api/reportpal, lists 19 lifts and 64 alpine trails for the three areas, rated beginner, intermediate, advanced or expert), as the combined map's were on 2026-11-10 (the same map files, and the OpenStreetMap data in the window the combined map's, an answer pinned to its timestamp being the same, element for element). OSM's easy, intermediate and advanced are the maps' green, blue and one diamond. Of the 74 named in-bounds runs in OSM, the report rates 49 by the same name and the maps label most of the rest; all carry the resort's rating but six: Main Chute (Summit West) and Broadway (Central), rated only by the printed map, Silver Fir's lower run and the lower West to Central crossover, rated only by the report, and Hyak Face and Hidden Valley (East), where the maps and the report agree against OSM. Where OSM splits a run into pieces of different ratings and the map draws the split, OSM's pieces stay: Thunderbolt, Thunderbird and Wildside black above and blue below (the report's Lower Thunderbird and Lower Wildside are blue), and the run-outs to a lift base that the map draws among other runs' symbols (Blowdown's last 235 m and Sarrah's Run's last 313 m to the Rampart base, beside Creek Run's green, and Inspiration's 531 m groomed way from its glade down Tanner's Pass's blue route). The blue way OSM names Julie's on the Pacific Crest side of the Julie's chair keeps OSM's intermediate: the Summit West map draws it as an unlabelled blue line (its green JULIES label is on the other way); the report's Easy Rider, a blue Summit West run not in OSM, may be it, but no source says so. Names from the map and the report: Dino's Revenge for an 80 m piece with a stray full stop. Names that differ only by a space, an abbreviation or a suffix stay as OSM has them (Hogwild, which the report spells Hog Wild; Chickamin, Chikamin in the report; Outback for the report's Upper and Lower Outback; the crossovers by OSM's names; the lifts without the report's Chair and Express suffixes). Runs OSM names that neither the maps nor the report do stay with OSM's rating (Bonanza, Chicken Nugget, Nugget Trail, Silver Nugget Bowl, nugget connector., Eclipse Bowl and its traverse, Wildside Cat Track, 360 Bowl Access and Inter-Summit 90). Parks: Central Park and Greenhorn Acres, the report's two terrain parks, are snow parks in OSM and carry the park flag already. Lifts: all 19 of the report's for the three areas are in OSM (Summit West 8, Summit Central 8, Summit East 3) and no lift name repeats across them or with Alpental's, so none takes its area's name. Hidden: the Tubing Park's covered conveyor and Snow Train, a nordic trail tagged nordic;downhill. The Summit Nordic Center's 109 cross-country ways, 20 hike, 12 ski-touring and 2 sledding ways (the Hyak sledding hill and the Tubing Center) are left out by the type rule. OSM gaps (shipped as at Palisades Tahoe): Easy Rider (Summit West, blue on the report) and Mom's (Summit East, blue on the report) are not in OSM, nor is Squirrel's Forest, the tree area the Hidden Valley inset names between Solitude and Revelation.

overrides.reason: Main Chute is a single black diamond (Most Difficult) on The Summit's Summit West trail map (summitatsnoqualmie.com/trail-maps) (black label with the diamond, between Thunderbolt and Thunderbird below the Wildside top); OSM rates it intermediate. The report does not list it, so the printed map decides.

Broadway is green (Easiest) on The Summit's Summit Central trail map (summitatsnoqualmie.com/trail-maps) (green label and dot below Top Traverse); OSM rates it intermediate. The report does not list it, so the printed map decides.

The lower Silver Fir run, from the bottom of Silver Fir Face to the Silver Fir lift's base, rated easy in OSM: its lift and trail report (summitatsnoqualmie.com/mountain-report) rates Silver Fir - Lower More Difficult, and the Summit Central trail map (summitatsnoqualmie.com/trail-maps) draws a blue square beside the lower lift line (its black SILVER FIR label is the face below the lift top, OSM's Silver Fir Face). Only the report rates the run by name, and it is the harder.

The lower crossover from Summit West to Central (the Lower Crossover the maps draw as an inter-summit trail, with no rating symbol): its lift and trail report (summitatsnoqualmie.com/mountain-report) rates West to Central Lower Most Difficult; OSM rates it intermediate. Only the report rates it, and it is the harder.

Hyak Face is a single black diamond on The Summit's Summit East trail map (summitatsnoqualmie.com/trail-maps) (black label with a diamond, below the East Peak top) and Most Difficult on its lift and trail report (summitatsnoqualmie.com/mountain-report); OSM rates it intermediate. The resort's sources agree, so they win.

Hidden Valley (the run) is a single black diamond on the Hidden Valley - East Backside inset of The Summit's Summit East trail map (summitatsnoqualmie.com/trail-maps) (black label beside the Hidden Valley lift) and Most Difficult on its lift and trail report (summitatsnoqualmie.com/mountain-report); OSM rates it intermediate. The resort's sources agree, so they win.

A stray full stop: the 80 m bottom piece of Dino's Revenge, which The Summit's Summit East trail map (summitatsnoqualmie.com/trail-maps) and its lift and trail report (summitatsnoqualmie.com/mountain-report) name DINO'S REVENGE (Most Difficult, as OSM rates it); OSM has Dino's Revenge. (with a full stop), so the map would label it as another run.

The Tubing Park's covered conveyor south of SR 906 at Summit Central (unnamed in OSM, outside the resort's polygons): The Summit's Summit Central trail map (summitatsnoqualmie.com/trail-maps) draws it at the Tubing Park, a tubing area, not ski terrain, and its lift and trail report (summitatsnoqualmie.com/mountain-report) does not list it among the lifts; hidden, as Vail's and Keystone's tubing carpets are.

Snow Train, a trail of the Summit Nordic Center on Forest Road 9070-110 (network SummitNordic, piste:type nordic;downhill in OSM) beside Summit East: its lift and trail report (summitatsnoqualmie.com/mountain-report) lists Snow Train under Nordic, and the alpine maps do not draw it. The type rule leaves the nordic centre out, and only its second type would keep this 99 m piece as a run.

Slot Couloir, a backcountry couloir on Snoqualmie Mountain's south face above Alpental (piste:grooming=backcountry, in no ski-area polygon): Alpental's terrain, about 1 km north of the box, which the alpental pack draws out of bounds. Alpental is a separate ski area of the same resort, on its own map (the owner's rule, 2026-11-14), and a listed neighbour of this map, but the couloir lies more than 250 m from Alpental's polygon, so the neighbour rule would keep it here as an out-of-bounds run of The Summit's: hidden, so that nothing of Alpental draws on The Summit's map.

Chair Peak North Face Descent, a backcountry line off Chair Peak behind Alpental's Back Bowls (piste:grooming=backcountry, in no ski-area polygon): Alpental's terrain, about 1 km north of the box's north-west corner, which the alpental pack draws out of bounds. Alpental is a separate ski area of the same resort, on its own map (the owner's rule, 2026-11-14), and a listed neighbour of this map, but the line lies more than 250 m from Alpental's and Alpental Backcountry's polygons, so the neighbour rule would keep it here as an out-of-bounds run of The Summit's: hidden, so that nothing of Alpental draws on The Summit's map.
